question: If a machine does 500 J of work in 4 seconds, what is its power output?
solution:
The correct answer is __**125 watt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Power** is defined as the rate at which work is done or energy is transferred.
 
• The formula to calculate power is **Power = Work / Time**.
 
• In this case, the work done is 500 joules and the time taken is 4 seconds.
 
• Using the formula, the power output is **500 J / 4 s = 125 watts**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Joule (J)**: The SI unit of work or energy. One joule is the amount of work done when a force of one newton displaces an object by one meter in the direction of the force.
 
• **Watt (W)**: The SI unit of power. One watt is equal to one joule per second.
 
• **Energy**: The capacity to do work. It can exist in various forms such as kinetic, potential, thermal, electrical, chemical, and nuclear energy.
 
• **SI Units**: The International System of Units (SI) is the modern form of the metric system and the world's most widely used system of measurement.
